raw_query: Search the Red Hat knowledge base for articles about the OpenShift authentication cluster operator being degraded with the error "OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerAvailable: Get https://oauth-openshift.../healthz: context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)". enhanced_query: OpenShift cluster operator degraded "OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerAvailable" "context deadline exceeded" console "DeploymentAvailable: 0 replicas"
answer:
Based on the Red Hat Knowledge Base, the symptoms you describe — the `authentication` Cluster Operator reporting `OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerAvailable: ... context deadline exceeded` and the `console` Cluster Operator reporting a rollout failure (`0 replicas available`) — are almost always seen **together** (often with `ingress` degraded too), and share common root causes. Below is a summary of what these conditions mean and the most relevant KB articles for diagnosis.

## What the symptoms indicate

- **`OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerAvailable / ...Degraded` with `context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`** — The authentication operator cannot reach the OAuth server's public route health endpoint, e.g. `https://oauth-openshift.apps.<cluster>/healthz`. This is an end-to-end reachability failure: DNS → external load balancer → ingress/router → oauth pod.

- **Console `DeploymentAvailable: 0 replicas` (or `SyncLoopRefreshProgressing: ... 0 replicas available`)** — The `openshift-console` deployment cannot roll out even 1 ready replica, so the console operator is not Available. Because the console is only reachable through the same `.apps` route/ingress path, the two problems are frequently the same underlying infrastructure/network issue, although the console rollout can also fail independently (image pulls, node issues, resource limits, etc.).

## Most relevant Red Hat KB articles

**1. Route health-check failures with "Client.Timeout exceeded" (directly matches your `authentication` message):**
- [Authentication, console and ingress operator are degraded with the error "Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6968984) — shows the exact `OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerAvailable: ... context deadline exceeded` message alongside console route health failures.
- [Unable to login to the cluster with cluster operators authentication, console and ingress marked as degraded](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7104755)
- [Authentication, Console and Ingress cluster operator goes into degraded state after updating the external DNS server on nodes via NNCP](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7135635) — covers the DNS-resolution variant (`dial tcp: lookup ... server misbehaving`).
- [[RHOCP 4] Ingress Cluster Operator degraded, Canary route fails to resolve from any/all OpenShift dns-default pods](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7049151)

**2. External load balancer / infrastructure causes:**
- [OpenShift installation fails with degraded authentication, console, and ingress operators with "Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers" when using an external Load Balancer](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7146953) — key diagnostic: bypass the LB and curl the ingress router pod IPs directly; if that returns 200, the LB VIP is the problem.
- [Cluster operators degraded with 503 errors due to NPAR settings on VMware ESXi hosts in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7142575) — VMware NIC partitioning misconfiguration causing `context deadline exceeded` on authentication/console/monitoring.
- [Cluster operators authentication, console, and ingress get degraded after changing F5 load balancer type](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7132917)

**3. Proxy configuration causes:**
- [Failing console and authentication operators in OpenShift 4 with ProxyConfigControllerDegraded](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6965526)
- [OpenShift Authentication Operator in Degraded state with ProxyConfigControllerDegraded after configuring a custom certificate for OAuth server URL](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7073329)

**4. Console specifically stuck at 0 replicas / not rolling out:**
- [Console operator shows degraded after installing Loki operator in RHOCP4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7042823) — shows the `SyncLoopRefreshProgressing: Working toward version ... 0 replicas available` pattern.
- [Operator hanging - too many replica sets preventing upgrade](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6344021) — console degraded because a deployment can't match desired replicas (runaway/revision pile-up).
- [Console operator is in degraded state with pods in ImagePullBackOff error in RHOCP4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7122061) — image pull failures leave console pods unavailable.
- [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform web console pods constantly being redeployed](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7141530)
- [Cluster Console is not accessible](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7107574) — authentication/console/ingress all degraded, console down.

## Suggested diagnostic steps

To pinpoint which of the above root causes applies, Red Hat's articles recommend roughly this path:

1. **Get the full operator status** to see all failing conditions:
   ```
   oc get co
   oc get co authentication -o yaml
   oc get co console -o yaml
